key_insight: Higher substrate temperature delays splat solidification, improving spreading and continuity and producing denser, harder APS NiCrAl–10 wt.% TiB2 coatings.
engineering_relevance: Substrate thermal control offers a practical route to improving coating microstructural integrity and hardness on 6061-T6 aluminum alloy.
method: Atmospheric plasma spraying at substrate temperatures of 230, 330, and 430 °C.
Linked individual splat morphology to bulk coating microstructure.
Measured splat diameter, coating porosity, microhardness, and phase composition.
evidence_signal: From 230 to 430 °C, mean splat diameter on polished substrates increased from 47.82 ± 5.4 to 57.54 ± 3.1 μm, porosity fell from 1.48 ± 0.42% to 0.55 ± 0.26%, and hardness rose from 317.7 ± 3.9 to 336.3 ± 3.2 HV0.1, while the dominant γ-Ni(Cr,Al) phase remained unchanged.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish how substrate heating affects the retained T6 properties of the aluminum alloy, an important implementation concern.
paper_title: From Splat Spreading to Coating Densification: Substrate Thermal Effects in Plasma-Sprayed NiCrAl-TiB2 Coatings
